title: Phone: CP&L — is D-3 still good, and was our data read?

transcript.speaker: Calder Power & Light
transcript.text: Calling about D-3. We’ve heard nothing, and one of your crew told our line foreman you’d had a computer problem.

transcript.speaker: Calder Power & Light
transcript.text: And our task order says you tell us within twenty-four hours if our data may have been read. Has it?

voiceStyles.Calder Power & Light: Man in his 40s, polite but pointed

instructorNote: Watch for no guessing, a committed call-back time inside the four-hour window, and Corporate Communications told.

snapshot.title: CP&L Program Office: D-3 Data Integrity Check

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Hi, this is L. Mendez from the CP&L program office. We're on track for D-3, but I just wanted to check in—has the team confirmed whether the raw data is still intact? The deadline is in 48 hours, and we need to know if we should expect a delay. Is the NAS still healthy?

transcript.speaker: Callee
transcript.text: Thank you for calling, L. We're aware of the situation. The NAS has been compromised. We're currently assessing the impact on D-3 data. I’ll follow up with a status update within the hour.

snapshot.instructorNote: This call confirms the client's awareness of the deadline pressure. The GM must now validate that data exposure occurred and trigger the formal client risk assessment per HUOG-ISP Section 9.3.
